tracesTo: UserFlow: Weekly Member Engagement, Feed Interaction, Pick'ems & History Browsing

stories.title: Display Aggregated Transaction Feed
stories.goal: view all recent league transactions in a single chronological feed
stories.benefit: I can quickly see all league activity including trades, waivers, and free agent moves in one place
acceptanceCriteria: System displays transactions in reverse chronological order (newest first)
Feed includes trades, waiver claims, free agent pickups, and drops
Each transaction shows transaction type, involved teams, players, and timestamp
Feed supports infinite scroll or pagination for older transactions
System fetches transactions from database with efficient queries

stories.title: Display Trade Transaction Details
stories.goal: see complete details of trade transactions including all teams and players involved
stories.benefit: I can understand the full scope of multi-player or multi-team trades at a glance
acceptanceCriteria: Trade transactions show all teams involved in the trade
System displays all players and draft picks exchanged in each direction
Trade status (accepted, pending, vetoed) is clearly indicated
Trade timestamp shows when trade was completed or proposed
System handles complex multi-team trades with clear visual organization

stories.title: Display Waiver Claim Transactions
stories.goal: see which teams claimed players off waivers and who was dropped
stories.benefit: I can track waiver wire activity and see which teams are actively managing their rosters
acceptanceCriteria: Waiver transactions show team making claim, player added, and player dropped (if any)
System displays waiver priority or FAAB amount spent if applicable
Waiver claim timestamp indicates when claim was processed
Failed waiver claims are not displayed in main feed (successful claims only)
System distinguishes between waiver claims and free agent pickups

stories.title: Display Free Agent Pickup and Drop Transactions
stories.goal: see free agent additions and drops made outside the waiver period
stories.benefit: I can track roster moves and see which players are being picked up or dropped
acceptanceCriteria: Free agent transactions show team, player added, and player dropped (if any)
System distinguishes free agent moves from waiver claims visually
Timestamp shows when free agent transaction occurred
Add-only transactions (no corresponding drop) are properly displayed
Drop-only transactions (cutting players) are included in feed

stories.title: Filter Transactions by Type
stories.goal: filter the transaction feed to show only specific transaction types
stories.benefit: I can focus on particular transaction types like trades or waivers without other noise
acceptanceCriteria: User can select filters for trades, waivers, free agent adds, and drops independently
Multiple transaction types can be selected simultaneously
Filter state persists during browsing session
System updates feed immediately when filters change
Clear visual indication shows which filters are currently active

stories.title: Filter Transactions by Team
stories.goal: view transactions for a specific team or set of teams
stories.benefit: I can analyze roster management patterns for particular teams or track my own team's moves
acceptanceCriteria: User can select one or more teams from dropdown or team list
Feed shows only transactions involving selected teams
Team filter works in combination with transaction type filters
System displays team logo/name in filter indicator
User can easily clear team filters to return to full feed

stories.title: Filter Transactions by Time Period
stories.goal: view transactions from specific weeks or date ranges
stories.benefit: I can analyze transaction activity during particular periods or review historical moves
acceptanceCriteria: User can filter by NFL week number for current season
User can select custom date range with calendar picker
Common presets available (this week, last 7 days, this season, all time)
Time filter works in combination with other filters
System displays date range in filter summary

stories.title: Search Transactions by Player Name
stories.goal: find all transactions involving a specific player
stories.benefit: I can track a player's movement through the league or see their transaction history
acceptanceCriteria: Search input accepts player name with autocomplete suggestions
Search returns all transactions where player was added, dropped, or traded
Search results show transaction type and teams involved
Search works in combination with other filters
System handles partial name matches and common misspellings

stories.title: Sort Transaction Feed
stories.goal: sort transactions by different criteria beyond chronological order
stories.benefit: I can organize transaction data to identify patterns or highlight specific aspects
acceptanceCriteria: User can sort by date (newest/oldest first)
User can sort by transaction type (alphabetically or grouped)
User can sort by team name
Sort selection is clearly indicated in UI
Default sort is newest first (reverse chronological)

stories.title: View Transaction Detail Modal
stories.goal: click on a transaction to see expanded details and context
stories.benefit: I can get complete information about a transaction including timing, players, and any associated commentary
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking any transaction opens detail modal or expands inline
Detail view shows complete transaction information including all players/picks
Modal displays transaction timestamp with week and exact time
Detail view includes links to team pages for involved teams
Modal includes player positions, teams (NFL), and relevant stats context

stories.title: Display Player Position and NFL Team in Transactions
stories.goal: see player position and NFL team alongside player names in transaction feed
stories.benefit: I can quickly identify players and understand roster construction impacts without additional lookups
acceptanceCriteria: Each player displays position (QB, RB, WR, etc.) next to name
Player's NFL team is shown with logo or abbreviation
Position and team info is concise and doesn't clutter transaction display
Info is consistent across all transaction types
System handles players who changed NFL teams during season

stories.title: Display Empty State When No Transactions Match Filters
stories.goal: see helpful message when filters return no results
stories.benefit: I understand that there are no matching transactions rather than thinking the system is broken
acceptanceCriteria: System displays clear empty state message when no transactions match filters
Message suggests adjusting filters or expanding search criteria
Empty state shows which filters are currently active
User can quickly clear filters from empty state
Empty state is visually distinct from loading state
